title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. According to Genesis 1:27, human beings were created in the what of God? (1 mark)
   A. Name only
   B. Image
   C. Voice only
   D. Shadow

2. According to Philippians 4:8, what should Christians think about? (1 mark)
   A. Whatever hurts others
   B. Whatever is true, pure and lovely
   C. Whatever is unkind
   D. Whatever is false

3. A classmate is sitting alone and looks sad. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Sit with them and kindly ask what is wrong
   B. Tell others to avoid them
   C. Laugh at them
   D. Ignore them

4. What is a consequence? (1 mark)
   A. A result of what we choose
   B. A type of song
   C. A school subject
   D. A holiday

5. What does it mean to honour your parents? (1 mark)
   A. To respect them, obey them and thank them
   B. To hide from them
   C. To ignore them
   D. To argue with them

6. If the first adult you tell does not help you, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Give up
   B. Tell nobody
   C. Forget it
   D. Tell another trusted adult

7. What is an attribute of God? (1 mark)
   A. A holiday
   B. A song
   C. A kind of building
   D. A quality that describes what God is like

8. The Bible begins by telling us that God is: (1 mark)
   A. The Creator of heaven and earth
   B. A king of Egypt
   C. A farmer
   D. A teacher of the law

9. What does it mean to revere God? (1 mark)
   A. To ignore Him
   B. To fear Him only
   C. To respect Him deeply and be in awe of Him
   D. To forget Him

10. Which book comes directly after Genesis? (1 mark)
   A. Leviticus
   B. Numbers
   C. Joshua
   D. Exodus

11. How much would Zacchaeus pay back to anyone he had cheated? (1 mark)
   A. Four times the amount
   B. Twice
   C. Ten times
   D. Half

12. Which word best describes a person who is honest even when nobody sees? (1 mark)
   A. Greed
   B. Jealousy
   C. Integrity
   D. Pride

13. Who asked Balaam to curse the Israelites? (1 mark)
   A. Joshua
   B. Herod
   C. Pharaoh
   D. King Balak

14. What should we do instead of cursing or speaking ill about others? (1 mark)
   A. Gossip
   B. Insult
   C. Spread rumours
   D. Speak well of them and bless them

15. Which people did Balak want Balaam to curse? (1 mark)
   A. The Egyptians
   B. The Israelites
   C. The Romans
   D. The Philistines

16. What does the story of Samson mainly show? (1 mark)
   A. The size of Timnah
   B. The power of lions
   C. The wealth of Philistines
   D. God's power

17. What does the name Abraham point to? (1 mark)
   A. Wise man
   B. Father of many nations
   C. Shepherd
   D. King of Egypt

18. Whom did the angel say was expecting a child in old age? (1 mark)
   A. Hannah
   B. Sarah
   C. Ruth
   D. Elizabeth

19. What did Mary answer to the angel's message? (1 mark)
   A. Leave me
   B. I do not believe you
   C. I must ask the king
   D. I am the Lord's servant, may your word to me be fulfilled

20. What does the name Jesus mean? (1 mark)
   A. Father of many
   B. Gift
   C. Great king
   D. The Lord saves

21. Which of these helps to protect our eyes? (1 mark)
   A. Reading in the dark
   B. Staring at the sun
   C. Not rubbing them with dirty hands
   D. Throwing dust

22. What does the lost coin stand for? (1 mark)
   A. A person who has wandered from God
   B. A lamp
   C. A house
   D. A rich man

23. Which verse says that God so loved the world? (1 mark)
   A. Luke 1:37
   B. Genesis 1:1
   C. Acts 2:38
   D. John 3:16

24. Why does a truthful person feel peaceful? (1 mark)
   A. They are rich
   B. They are popular
   C. They have nothing to hide
   D. They are old

25. What should you do if you broke a cup? (1 mark)
   A. Run away
   B. Hide it
   C. Tell the truth and say sorry
   D. Blame a sibling

26. Why should we obey teachers? (1 mark)
   A. They are our enemies
   B. To be punished
   C. They guide us and help us learn
   D. For fun

27. What should you do if an adult tells you to do something that hurts you? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it
   B. Hide it
   C. Obey
   D. Refuse and tell a trusted adult

28. Which is a personal item? (1 mark)
   A. The school gate
   B. A school uniform
   C. A classroom desk
   D. A library book

29. Which of these is a result of sin? (1 mark)
   A. It separates us from God
   B. It brings praise
   C. It brings peace
   D. It brings health

30. Which helps you to avoid situations that lead to sin? (1 mark)
   A. Choosing good friends
   B. Going to wrong places
   C. Ignoring parents
   D. Keeping bad secrets

31. Which action honours God with the body? (1 mark)
   A. Taking drugs
   B. Using bad words
   C. Fighting
   D. Keeping clean and eating well

32. Why should we take part in church activities? (1 mark)
   A. To grow spiritually and serve others
   B. To waste time
   C. To avoid home
   D. To show off

33. Why did Jesus drive out the buyers and sellers? (1 mark)
   A. They were poor
   B. They were misusing God's house
   C. They were children
   D. They were noisy

34. What did the first Christians devote themselves to? (1 mark)
   A. Fighting
   B. Travel
   C. Trading
   D. Teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer

35. Who replaced Judas among the twelve? (1 mark)
   A. Stephen
   B. Matthias
   C. Paul
   D. Barnabas

36. Who was watching when Stephen was stoned? (1 mark)
   A. Peter
   B. Thomas
   C. A young man named Saul
   D. Balaam

37. What does the word Christian mean? (1 mark)
   A. A priest
   B. A rich person
   C. A soldier
   D. A follower of Christ

38. In Matthew 6:5-6, how did Jesus say we should pray? (1 mark)
   A. Sincerely, not to be seen by others
   B. Never
   C. Loudly to impress
   D. Only in public

39. Why does the prayer use "our" and "us"? (1 mark)
   A. We pray together and for others
   B. Only for adults
   C. Only for priests
   D. It is a mistake

40. What does "Give us today our daily bread" mean? (1 mark)
   A. We ask God for what we need each day
   B. We ask for a party
   C. We ask for gold
   D. We ask for money

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain how John the Baptist prepared the way for Jesus and what we can learn about living righteously. (5 marks)

42. Give two lessons from the story of Balaam and his donkey. (2 marks)

43. Describe what a child should do after sinning, in four steps. (4 marks)

44. What did Pharaoh's two dreams mean? (2 marks)

45. Describe Joseph's plan to save Egypt from the famine. (4 marks)

46. Explain the meaning of the word disciple. (2 marks)

47. State two promises that God made to Abram in Genesis 12:1-3. (2 marks)

48. Explain what the parts of the parable stand for. (3 marks)

49. Describe what a child should do when they lose or break something belonging to someone else. (3 marks)

50. State two choices that you make at home every day. (2 marks)

51. Explain what a child should do if they are offered drugs or asked to do something that defiles the body. (5 marks)

52. Name two ways of showing compassion to a grieving neighbour. (2 marks)

53. Explain four ways of building self-control. (4 marks)

54. Explain why God changed Abram's name to Abraham. (3 marks)

55. Give two people you should pray for. (2 marks)

56. Give three rules for staying safe from strangers. (3 marks)

57. Describe four ways of growing the fruit of the Spirit. (4 marks)

58. Give two examples of school property. (2 marks)

59. Explain what the parable of the mustard seed teaches about God's kingdom. (3 marks)

60. Explain why Christians should help those in need. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Image
   Genesis 1:27 says that God created human beings in His own image.

2. B — Whatever is true, pure and lovely
   Philippians 4:8 lists true, noble, right, pure and lovely things.

3. A — Sit with them and kindly ask what is wrong
   Kindness and listening help a sad friend.

4. A — A result of what we choose
   A consequence is the result of a choice.

5. A — To respect them, obey them and thank them
   Honouring includes respect, obedience and thankfulness.

6. D — Tell another trusted adult
   Keep telling until someone helps.

7. D — A quality that describes what God is like
   An attribute is a quality that describes someone.

8. A — The Creator of heaven and earth
   Genesis 1:1 tells us God created heaven and earth.

9. C — To respect Him deeply and be in awe of Him
   Reverence is deep respect for God.

10. D — Exodus
   The order is Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy.

11. A — Four times the amount
   He promised to pay back four times.

12. C — Integrity
   Integrity means doing right when nobody is watching.

13. D — King Balak
   Numbers 22 says that Balak, king of Moab, sent for Balaam.

14. D — Speak well of them and bless them
   God's people are called to bless, not curse.

15. B — The Israelites
   Balak feared the Israelites camped on the plains of Moab.

16. D — God's power
   The Spirit of the Lord gave Samson strength.

17. B — Father of many nations
   God said that he would be a father of many nations.

18. D — Elizabeth
   Mary's relative Elizabeth was expecting a baby.

19. D — I am the Lord's servant, may your word to me be fulfilled
   Luke 1:38 records her humble answer.

20. D — The Lord saves
   Matthew 1:21 links His name to saving people from their sins.

21. C — Not rubbing them with dirty hands
   Clean hands protect the eyes from infection.

22. A — A person who has wandered from God
   The coin stands for a lost person.

23. D — John 3:16
   John 3:16 is the memory verse.

24. C — They have nothing to hide
   Truth brings a clear conscience.

25. C — Tell the truth and say sorry
   Honesty and apology are right.

26. C — They guide us and help us learn
   Teachers care for our progress and safety.

27. D — Refuse and tell a trusted adult
   Obedience is only for good instructions.

28. B — A school uniform
   Personal items belong to you.

29. A — It separates us from God
   Sin harms us and others.

30. A — Choosing good friends
   Good friends help us do right.

31. D — Keeping clean and eating well
   Care for the body honours God.

32. A — To grow spiritually and serve others
   Participation helps faith to grow.

33. B — They were misusing God's house
   The temple was for prayer, not trading.

34. D — Teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer
   Acts 2:42.

35. B — Matthias
   Acts 1:26 says Matthias was chosen.

36. C — A young man named Saul
   Acts 7:58.

37. D — A follower of Christ
   Christian means a follower of Christ.

38. A — Sincerely, not to be seen by others
   Jesus warned against showing off.

39. A — We pray together and for others
   The prayer reminds us to think of others.

40. A — We ask God for what we need each day
   It refers to daily needs.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: John preached in the wilderness, called people to repent and baptised them, so their hearts were ready for Jesus. We can learn to turn away from sin, be honest and kind, pray, and tell others about Jesus by our example.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for preaching, 1 for repentance, 1 for baptism or readiness, 1 for turning from sin, 1 for a righteous example.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Obey God; do not be greedy; bless others; be kind to animals. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid lesson.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Admit it, say sorry to God, say sorry to the person hurt, put things right, decide not to repeat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 4.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for plenty and 1 mark for famine.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Find a wise man to be in charge, take a fifth of the grain during the seven good years, store it in the towns, and use it in the famine years.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point up to 4.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: A follower and learner of Jesus.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for follower and 1 for learner.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: To make him a great nation, to bless him, to make his name great, and to bless all peoples through him.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid promise.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: The woman stands for God; the coin stands for a lost person; the joy stands for the joy in heaven when someone repents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid part.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tell the owner honestly, say sorry, offer to replace or repair it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: Whether to do chores, to obey parents, to share food, to be kind to siblings. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid choice.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Say no clearly, walk away, avoid the group, tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher, pray for strength, and choose friends who make good choices.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying no, 1 for walking away, 1 for telling an adult, 1 for prayer, 1 for good friends.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Visit, comfort, share food, pray with them. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid way.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Pray each morning, set small goals, keep busy with good activities, choose good friends, avoid tempting situations.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 4.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: God made a covenant with him and promised that he would be a father of many nations. The new name reminded him of this promise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the covenant, 1 for the promise, 1 for the name as a reminder.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Parents, guardians, friends, teachers, sick people, leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not go with them, do not accept gifts or lifts, do not give personal details, shout for help, tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid rule.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Pray, read the Bible, practise one fruit at a time, ask for encouragement, say sorry and try again.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 4.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Desks, textbooks, library books, toilets, compound.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: It began small, with Jesus and a few followers, but it grows large and gives shelter to many.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for small beginning, 1 for growth, 1 for shelter or many people.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jesus taught it; it shows love; it makes the community stronger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.
